//: Not a TypeScript project. This is `checkJs` pointed at plain JavaScript,
and it is deliberately NOT part of `npm run verify` or of CI.
Why it exists: the class of bug it sees is the one that has actually cost
this app time. `let editor = null` followed by `editor.state` in a function
reachable before the editor is built is a type error and nothing else —
eslint cannot see it, the bundler cannot see it, and three of them shipped
and threw on every launch for a fortnight.
Why it does not gate: run today it reports about 2,100 errors, of which
roughly 630 are that class (TS18047, 'possibly null') and roughly 900 are
the DOM's own typing — `querySelector` answers `Element`, so every
`.focus()` and `.value` on a result is an error until the code says which
kind of element it expects. Both are worth fixing and neither is worth
blocking a build on until they are. A gate that is red on the day it is
installed is a gate that gets turned off.
So: `npm run typecheck`, read the null-safety findings, fix them a module
at a time. What HOLDS a module once it is clean is `npm run typecheck:gate`
(scripts/typecheck-gate.mjs), which is in verify and in CI: it runs this
same config and fails on findings in a named list of already-clean modules,
44 of them today. It filters the OUTPUT rather than narrowing `include`,
because `include` does not mean 'report only these' — tsc reports on every
file it pulls into the program, so a clean module would fail for the errors
of a messy one it imports. Widen the list, do not loosen the config.
scripts/ and bench/ are left out on purpose: they are test harnesses, and
their job is to be thrown away and rewritten.
